summary.motive: Flood the middle of the field with two staggered deep crossers so zone drops cannot cover both layers.
summary.whyItWorks: Vertical stems remove the corners and hooks first; the crossers then arrive offset in time and depth, so whichever defender takes layer one abandons layer two.
summary.failureMode: The Mike sits in the middle hole without chasing either crosser, or man coverage lets defenders trade the crossers cleanly at the mesh point.

beats.title: 1. The Vertical Stems Set the Table
beats.text: The slot and flanker fire pure vertical releases, pinning the corners deep and forcing both hooks to turn their backs to the middle before any crossing route shows.

beats.title: 2. Layer One Departs
beats.text: At twenty yards the split end breaks off his stem into the deep cross-country lane. The free safety must now honor the deepest threat in his middle third.

beats.title: 3. Layer Two Crosses Underneath
beats.text: Four yards deeper and four seconds later, the tight end drives his fourteen-yard crosser directly beneath the first. The Mike is caught between layers.

beats.title: 4. The Distribution Throw
beats.text: With the free safety committed to the deep crosser and the Mike dragged to the boundary, the second crosser runs free across the middle for an easy completion.

relations.tell: Both inside receivers release instantly vertical and only break after passing twelve yards — shallow drags never appear in this series.
